# Object.assign Method

#### Course: Modern JavaScript Essentials

## Object.assign Method

Object.assign copies properties into the first object (the target) from other objects (the sources). It is commonly used to merge default settings with custom overrides, creating a single combined configuration.

For example,

```javascript
1const defaults = { speed: 3, color: "white", lives: 3 }; 
2const custom = { speed: 5, color: "blue" };
3
4const settings = Object.assign({}, defaults, custom);
5
6console.log(settings.speed); 
7console.log(settings.color); 
8console.log(settings.lives);
```

Here, Object.assign starts with an empty object {}, copies all properties from defaults, then overwrites with properties from custom. The speed and color from custom replace the defaults, while lives keeps its default value because custom does not define it.

It is also good practice to pass an empty object as the first argument. I always do that so I create a new object instead of changing the main source.
